title: Exceptional Cones from an Indefinite Bogoliubov Metric in Hyperbolic Polariton Condensates
authors: Junhui Cao, Kirill Bazarov, Alexey Kavokin
abstract: Long-wavelength Bogoliubov phonons in an ordinary condensate realize the standard acoustic Lorentz metric. We show that a condensate formed in a hyperbolic polariton band realizes a different collective geometry with an indefinite Bogoliubov metric whose spatial signature is inherited from the opposite signs of the band curvatures. This metric converts the acoustic light cone into a hyperbolic stability wedge, separating propagating quasiparticles from dynamically unstable ones. In a driven-dissipative condensate, gain saturation turns this metric relation into a non-Hermitian Bogoliubov dispersion. The zero-discriminant surface becomes an exceptional cone in the parametric space $(q_x,q_y,Δ_{\rm NH})$, appearing as an exceptional hyperbola at fixed gain saturation. Across this surface the Bogoliubov branches coalesce, the biorthogonal phase rigidity collapses, and the spectrum changes from propagation to amplified or overdamped dynamics. Our results identify hyperbolic polariton condensates as a controllable setting where non-Hermitian exceptional degeneracies are organized by an effective Bogoliubov metric.
summary: The paper investigates collective excitations in hyperbolic polariton condensates, finding that the underlying Bogoliubov metric is indefinite, unlike standard acoustic systems. This geometry dictates that gain saturation leads to an exceptional cone structure in parameter space. The study demonstrates that this framework allows for the controlled engineering and observation of non-Hermitian degeneracies using optical matter waves.
main_problem: To characterize the collective excitation geometry of a condensate formed in a hyperbolic polariton band, particularly how this relates to non-Hermitian exceptional degeneracies.
main_result: The system exhibits an indefinite Bogoliubov metric, causing the light cone to become a hyperbolic stability wedge. The resulting zero-discriminant surface forms a controllable exceptional cone/hyperbola structure in parameter space.
method: Analysis involves linearizing the driven-dissipative condensate equation and deriving effective quadratic metrics (Bogoliubov metric) that govern the dispersion relation across different regimes.
model_or_system: The system is modeled by a scalar driven-dissipative condensate equation describing hyperbolic polariton condensates. The physics is analyzed via Bogoliubov excitations, leading to non-Hermitian spectral analysis.
key_observables: Bogoliubov metric signature (indefinite), exceptional cone/hyperbola structure, eigenvalue splitting $|\omega_+ - \omega_-|$, and biorthogonal phase rigidity $r_+$.
important_parameters: Gain saturation ($\Delta_{NH}$), band curvatures ($\alpha_x\alpha_y < 0$), and interaction strength ($g$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the long-wavelength limit for deriving the effective metric, and it models the system using a driven-dissipative mean-field approach.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate spectral diagnostics showing the collapse of the particle spectral function onto the exact BdG hyperboloid near exceptional points (EPs), and real-space simulations show localized perturbations developing elongated, sign-alternating profiles aligned with unstable hyperbolic sectors.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing the standard acoustic metric in ordinary condensates to deriving the indefinite Bogoliubov metric for hyperbolic polaritons. It then incorporates gain saturation to introduce non-Hermiticity, leading to the identification and characterization of the exceptional cone structure via spectral analysis and real-space evolution.
why_interesting: This work directly connects geometric concepts (indefinite metrics) from condensed matter theory to topological features (exceptional degeneracies) in open quantum systems, providing a powerful framework for understanding non-Hermitian physics in controllable optical platforms like polaritons.
